note: Withdrawable fact pool for the IT-security scenario, seeded from public CISA advisory patterns (affected version, finding, mitigation, dates). Facts paraphrased; each record funds one distinct page.
sources: CISA cybersecurity/ICS advisories (cisa.gov) — credential/authentication findings and mitigations, public domain

records.description_body: The customer portal saw credential-stuffing traffic causing 1,240 unauthorized login attempts over a six hour window.
records.timeline_body: An anomalous login volume alarm fired at 22:58; the surge began at 23:05 and was contained after WAF rate-limiting at 05:10.
records.contributing_body: Auth-gateway 3.4.0 exposes a legacy login endpoint without rate limiting; adaptive throttling is disabled by default.
records.action: Upgrade to auth-gateway 3.5.2 on public portals, or enable adaptive throttling on 3.4.0.

records.description_body: The partner API gateway logged a default-credentials probe over a three hour window from a distributed source.
records.timeline_body: A default admin account created during deployment was targeted; no successful authentication was confirmed.
records.contributing_body: A default credentials configuration remained enabled on auth-gateway 3.4.1 after provisioning.
records.action: Rotate default credentials and disable the deployment admin account across gateways.

records.description_body: The employee SSO endpoint experienced token-replay attempts over a four hour window.
records.timeline_body: Authentication tokens were observed being reused; session binding checks flagged the anomaly.
records.contributing_body: Auth-gateway 3.3.9 kept authentication tokens in cleartext in process memory, enabling replay.
records.action: Upgrade to 3.5.2 which encrypts tokens in memory and enforces session binding.

records.description_body: The public status page login saw a low-volume brute-force attempt over a two hour window that lockout policy blunted.
records.timeline_body: Account lockout thresholds tripped after repeated failures; no accounts were compromised.
records.contributing_body: Rate limiting was absent on the legacy endpoint of auth-gateway 3.4.0, though lockout policy limited impact.
records.action: Add rate limiting to the legacy endpoint and add anomalous-login alerting.

records.description_body: The mobile app auth service saw distributed login attempts over a five hour window from residential proxies.
records.timeline_body: A device-fingerprint anomaly flagged the pattern; step-up authentication contained it.
records.contributing_body: Auth-gateway 3.4.2 lacked device-fingerprint checks on the mobile login path.
records.action: Enable device-fingerprint step-up on 3.5.2 for mobile auth.

records.description_body: The admin console login recorded a targeted attempt over a one hour window against two privileged accounts.
records.timeline_body: MFA challenges blocked the attempts; alerts escalated to the on-call analyst.
records.contributing_body: Legacy auth-gateway 3.3.8 permitted password-only fallback on the admin path.
records.action: Remove password-only fallback and enforce MFA on all privileged logins.

records.description_body: The billing portal login saw credential-stuffing over a three hour window overlapping a marketing campaign spike.
records.timeline_body: Elevated legitimate traffic masked the attack initially; correlation rules surfaced it after 40 minutes.
records.contributing_body: Rate limiting on auth-gateway 3.4.0 did not distinguish attack traffic from the campaign surge.
records.action: Tune rate limits with traffic-baseline awareness and upgrade to 3.5.2.

records.description_body: The internal wiki login logged a slow credential-spray over a four hour window from a single compromised host.
records.timeline_body: A low-and-slow pattern evaded per-minute thresholds; a daily-aggregate rule caught it.
records.contributing_body: Auth-gateway 3.4.1 rate windows were too short to catch low-and-slow spraying.
records.action: Add long-window aggregate rate detection and isolate the compromised host.
